title: Observability Conformance and Failover Certification Playbook
author: Morgan Reyes
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines a standardized certification process for enterprise onboarding focused on observability conformance and failover simulation. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable test-suite that validates a tenant's integration with Redwood's telemetry, alerting, and failover behaviors before and during go‑live.

Why this exists:
- Ensure consistent telemetry quality and signal availability for QBRs and SLO enforcement.
- Reduce post‑go‑live escalations by pre‑validating failure modes and remediation paths.
- Provide a clear sign‑off for both Customer Success and the customer’s engineering team.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Customer Success engineers (CSEs), Onboarding architects, Customer reliability engineers, SRE on-call.
- Applies to: Dedicated and Private tenants (VPC/on‑prem), customers with reserved capacity, and any Hosted customers requesting enterprise SLA/observability contracts.
- Not in scope: low‑volume self‑serve signups unless otherwise requested.

Certification objectives (pass criteria):
1) Observability conformance: required metrics, traces, and logs are present, correctly tagged, and within fidelity bounds.
2) Alert and paging behavior: alerts fire at configured thresholds and route to intended escalation targets.
3) Failover simulation: tenant can gracefully fallback to configured model‑variant and/or region policy without data loss or broken requests within SLOs.
4) Performance parity: tail latency and 95p token throughput are within 10% of the accepted baseline for the tenant profile.

Prerequisites (customer and Redwood):
- Customer provides: representative API keys, ingress IP ranges, and a traffic seed (synthetic workload or production snapshot).
- Contracted observability level agreed (metrics retention window, trace sampling rate).
- Access: cross-account metrics forwarding set up (if Dedicated/Private), service account for telemetry validation, and customer contact list for paging.
- Baseline established: a 24h baseline run capturing normal traffic characteristics and sequence length distribution.

Conformance test suite (run by CSE):
- Metrics coverage checklist (automated assertions):
  - Per-tenant request count (counter)
  - Per-model token count (counter)
  - Per-route 95th and 99th percent latency (histogram)
  - Inference errors by class (5xx, 4xx, model-timeout)
  - KV cache hit ratio (gauge)
  - Batching statistics (avg batch size, dropout count)
  - Memory/GC and GPU memory pressure (hosted or dedicated telemetry exporters)
- Tracing:
  - Root span includes route, model.id, request.id, tenant.id, and sequence_len tags.
  - KV cache warmup and cache-miss traces for long‑running sessions.
  - Downstream service spans (e.g., affinity proxy, telemetry bridge) present and correlated.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with keys: timestamp, severity, tenant_id, request_id, model_variant, error_code.

Telemetry assertion examples (fail/pass matrix):
- Metric emission: per-tenant request counter emits once per request -> pass if >=99.9% of sampled requests have metrics.
- Tag fidelity: model_variant tag present -> pass if present in >=99% of traces.
- Sampling: trace sampling at configured rate within ±2% of target.

Failover simulation scenarios (minimum required):
1) Model variant degradation: simulate a regression in primary model (increased generation time or error rate). Expected behavior: automatic traffic shift to fallback variant within configured rollout window; client-facing failures <=0.1% during switch.
2) Regional outage: simulate region R failover to R2. Expected behavior: DNS/Anycast routing handoff, warming of KV cache for hot prefixes, and latency impact within contractual SLOs (95p latency < 2x baseline or configured threshold).
3) GPU node eviction (Dedicated): simulate node preemption and validate autoscaler rehydration, batch redistribution, and request retry behavior.
4) Telemetry bridge loss: simulate loss of telemetry export for 5 minutes and validate local buffering, partial metrics backfill correctness, and alert suppression mechanisms.

Detailed runbook (step-by-step):
1) Preparation (T-72 to T-1 days):
  - T-72: Confirm prerequisites, sign OSS (if applicable), and create certification ticket in JIRA (label: obs-cert).
  - T-48: Customer provides traffic seed and auth tokens for test harness.
  - T-24: Baseline run completed and validated; acceptance thresholds documented.
  - T-1: Final smoke test and contact list validated.
2) Execution day (D):
  - 09:00: Kickoff call with stakeholders.
  - 09:30–11:00: Run observability conformance scripts (see commands below).
  - 11:00–12:30: Run failover scenario 1 (model variant). Monitor telemetry and collect traces.
  - 13:30–15:30: Run region failover simulation with staged traffic migration.
  - 15:30–16:30: Run node eviction and telemetry bridge tests.
  - 16:30–17:30: Analyze results, compile pass/fail, and agree next steps.
3) Post-exec (D+1 to D+7):
  - D+1: Deliver certification report and recommended remediations.
  - D+3–D+7: Re-run specific tests on fixes and mark items closed in certification ticket.

Automation commands and snippets (examples):
- Run metric smoke test (CLI):
```
redwoodctl observability assert --tenant $TENANT_ID --duration 15m --checks metrics,logs,traces --out results.yaml
```
- Inject model latency fault (test harness uses canary traffic):
```
redwoodctl inject fault --target model:$MODEL_ID --type delay --p50 200ms --p95 1200ms --duration 10m
```
- Simulate region drain (staged):
```
redwoodctl region failover --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --staged 50,75,100 --monitoring-window 5m
```

Pass/fail reporting and artifact collection:
- Artifacts required for sign-off: results.yaml (assertions), raw trace archive (.zip), sample logs (masked PII), screenshots of dashboards showing baseline vs test windows, and a short executive summary (1 page).
- Pass requires: all high-priority conformance checks passed AND no more than 2 medium severity failover gaps (with tied remediation plan).

Remediation and escalation matrix:
- Severity classification:
  - P0: cert-blocker (missing tenant id tags, missing request counter, or failover causes >1% client errors) -> Engineering oncall + CSE triage within 1 hour.
  - P1: degraded observability signals (missing noncritical tags, sampling misalignment) -> Owner team fix within 72 hours.
  - P2: cosmetic issues (logging format differences) -> backlog item for future patch.
- Escalation flow: CSE -> Platform Oncall -> Runtime Engineering -> Head of SRE. Use the internal pager channel #obs-cert-paging for P0.

Sign-off and handover:
- Sign-off stakeholders: Customer Success Manager, Customer Reliability Lead, Onboarding Architect, and SRE certifier.
- Sign-off artifact: single JSON certificate stored in the ticket with fields: tenant_id, cert_date, results_uri, signer_emails, scope (observability/failover), and expiry (90 days).

Operational notes and cautions:
- For Private deployments with air-gapped telemetry, ensure local artifact encryption and transfer controls are in place.
- Avoid running production traffic seeding during business critical windows; prefer weekend or agreed maintenance windows.
- When simulating paid capacity changes (autoscaler stress), ensure commercial approval for potential billing spikes.

Ownership and contacts:
- Playbook owner: Morgan Reyes (Customer Success – Observability Lead).
- Primary engineering contact: Kai Huang (Runtime Engineering).
- SRE escalation: Oncall rotation (see /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/oncall-rotation).

Templates and checklists (appendix):
- Preflight checklist (checkbox list):
  - [ ] Traffic seed uploaded and validated
  - [ ] Cross-account metrics forwarding configured
  - [ ] Pager rotations updated
  - [ ] Baseline run completed
  - [ ] JIRA ticket created and stakeholders invited
- Certification report template (fields to populate):
  - Tenant ID, Customer contact, Certification date, Tests run, Pass/fail summary, Remediation items, Signers.

QBR integration and recurring validation:
- If certified, tenant will be enrolled in a quarterly telemetry health check. The certification expiry triggers a reminder 30 days before expiry to schedule a re-certification window. Failures found during QBR health checks feed back into the remediation board and may require out-of-band recertification.
